title: Does multivariate (conditional) transfer entropy recover the XOR synergy blind spot, and then equal Phi? — H_290 / paper follow-up
question: Does multivariate conditional TE recover the bivariate XOR blind spot (rules 150/105), and does it then track Phi better than bivariate TE (r=0.883)?
engine: HEXAD/IIT4/lib (reused): iit4_eca.eca_tpm + iit4_bigphi.big_phi + iit4_bit/iit4_pow2 (via stdlib/consciousness). TEm_i = H(next_i | self_i) joint-count inline.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)
toolchain_note: built via fix-1180 bypass: HEXA_MAC_BUILD_OK=1 HEXA_LANG=<root> hexa.real.bak-2026-05-22-pre-no-hxc build <src> -o <bin>.
metric_def: TEm_total = sum_i H(next_i | self_i) over uniform 2^n ensemble = multivariate conditional transfer entropy from all other inputs to i given i's own present (deterministic substrate). bits.
seed_hypothesis_H1: (a) XOR rules 150/105 TEm>0 (recovered from bivariate 0), 204 stays 0; (b) Pearson r(TEm, Phi) >= 0.883.

rule_90.note: OVER-PREDICTION: flow without integration (Phi=0); same rule LZ over-predicts (H_288)

criteria.C2_r_IMPROVE: NOT MET -> PARTIAL (r=0.705 < 0.883; recovery did NOT improve Phi-tracking)

falsifiers.F293_2_r_VERDICT: clause(b) NOT MET  (r=0.705412 < 0.883 — recovery != Phi-tracking improvement)

verdict_class: H1 PARTIAL (synergy recovered, Phi-tracking not improved -> Phi stays distinct)
finding: Multivariate (conditional) transfer entropy RECOVERS the bivariate XOR synergy blind spot (rules 150/105: bivariate TE=0 -> multivariate TEm=4.0; identity 204 stays 0) but does NOT improve Phi-tracking: the correlation DROPS from r=0.883 (bivariate) to r=0.705 (multivariate, Spearman 0.681). The cause is a NEW over-prediction: rule 90 receives flow from neighbours (TEm=4.0) but the system is reducible, so Phi=0 — multivariate TE over-counts NON-INTEGRATED flow. Thus NO order of classical transfer entropy equals Phi: bivariate under-counts synergy (150/105), multivariate over-counts non-integrated flow (90). This strengthens the paper's thesis (Phi is a distinct integration measure, not a fixed-order flow statistic) and empirically REFINES the paper's section-future prediction that multivariate TE would raise the correlation above 0.88 (recovery confirmed, raise refuted). Rule 90 fails for BOTH LZ (H_288) and multivariate TE here = cross-measure signature of 'flow/complexity without integration'.
honest_limits: L1: TEm_i = H(next_i|self_i) is ONE multivariate-conditional-TE form (all-other-inputs given self); per-source conditional TE / PID synergy-term separation would decompose differently.
L2 (rule 90 over-prediction, key): TEm over-predicts rule 90 (4.0 at Phi=0); same rule LZ over-predicts (H_288) -> cross-measure 'non-integrated flow' signature.
L3: Phi_mean state-averaged -> direction trusted, magnitude hedged.
L4: n=4 small, 10-rule panel -> direction robust, exact r panel-dependent.
L5: ECA = flow/integration proxy, not phenomenal claim.
L6: structure-cut big-Phi; correlation conclusion robust to scale offset.
L7: verdict is a toy-substrate measurement fact.

verify_fence.claim: H_293 multivariate (conditional) transfer entropy recovers the XOR synergy blind spot of bivariate TE (rules 150/105: 0 -> 4.0) but does NOT improve Phi-tracking (r 0.883 -> 0.705): it over-predicts on rule 90 (flow without integration, Phi=0). No order of classical transfer entropy equals Phi; deterministic toy-substrate, NOT an atlas identity
